div.div: أَيَّامٌ مُعْتَذِلَاتٌ (tropical:) Intensely hot days; (S, O, K, TA;) as also ↓ عُذُلٌ ; (K;) as though they blamed one another; one saying to another, “ I am hotter than thou, and why is not thy heat like my heat? ” (TA:) or, accord. to IAar, ↓ العُذُلُ signifies the hot days. (O.) And مُعْتَذِلَاتُ سُهَيْلٍ (tropical:) Certain intensely hot days that come before the [auroral] rising of Suheyl [i. e. Canopus], or after it; so called as [though] meaning that they blame one another (↓ يَتَعَاذَلْنَ ), and bid one another to be intensely hot or to desist from heat: and also called مُعْتَدِلَات [q. v.], with the unpointed د, as being equal in intensity of heat. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
